title: More Than One Thing: the Plural Accusative -ket

sections.content: When the object is plural, the accusative suffix becomes -ket (or -ok/-ek/-öket after a plural marker), attached after the plural ending. film ('film'), pluralized and then made accusative, gives filmeket ('films', as object).

items.spanish: Szeretem a zenét és a filmeket.

sections.content: Build plural accusative in two steps: first the plural (film -> filmek), then the accusative (filmek -> filmeket). Trying to skip straight from film to a plural-accusative form usually produces the wrong linking vowel.
